counterexamples.B1: caller claim session-X + producer evidence session-Y -> claim stays SESSION_CLAIMED_UNVERIFIED, only session-Y is producer-supported, the disagreement remains visible
counterexamples.B2: an association naming a different Attempt -> UNRESOLVED / ATTEMPT_MISMATCH
counterexamples.B3: an association bound to a different Invocation -> UNRESOLVED / INVOCATION_MISMATCH
counterexamples.B4: the same evidence delivered four times (including a retry reference) -> ONE binding, one session identity, one invocation
counterexamples.B5: one invocation reported with two Session identities -> UNRESOLVED / CONFLICTING_SESSION_IDENTITY, and reversing the input gives the identical refusal (no first-wins or last-wins)
counterexamples.B6: a producer observation with durableBindingRef=null -> UNRESOLVED / DURABLE_BINDING_MISSING; the observation is still represented
counterexamples.B7: no association evidence at all, however readable a session is -> UNRESOLVED / NO_ASSOCIATION_EVIDENCE; the resolver has no readability input
counterexamples.B8: a caller-declared association -> UNRESOLVED / NOT_PRODUCER_OBSERVED; the ordinary Preview performs zero reads and reports no verified SessionId and no admitted events

cardinality: Attempt -> Invocation(s) -> Session(s) is representable; a conflicting pair is refused rather than silently overwritten, and a retry reference for the same identity does not create a second binding
verdict: PASS — every §8.7 counterexample has deterministic, fail-closed semantics
